task/instruction.md:9 mandates Node.js, Express and SQLite; environment/instructions/integration.md:3-8 further mandates better-sqlite3. task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:3 forbids source/file inspection, and the only restart criterion tests durability, not SQLite or Express. A browser-identical implementation using a different backend can earn full credit despite an explicit implementation requirement.
quality.counterexample: A submission with an in-memory or JSON-file Node server, or a different server framework, can present identical UI/HTTP behavior and receive full browser credit despite the explicit Express/SQLite mandate.
quality.suggested_fix: Remove task-added backend-technology mandates that cannot be browser-verified, or provide a permitted independent architecture check without changing shared browser-only policy.

task/tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml requires cross-context readback but not process restart; task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml hro_restart has only weight 0.5 of 45.0 functional points. An otherwise complete in-memory server can pass the gates and nearly every scored row while discarding all work on restart.
quality.counterexample: Implement all observable economics in process memory and pass the cross-browser-context gate; restart loses all records, but only hro_restart fails, losing 0.0067 total reward.
quality.suggested_fix: Make durable successful write plus restart/readback part of a meaningful gate or give persistence enough independent mass to keep a memory-only implementation low.

quality.evidence: task/tests/scoring.toml:1-11 is numerically shaped and functional has 77 binary criteria, but no measured weak/partial app run or full configured judge log establishes score spread.
task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml uses binary behavioral rows; scored/visual/judge.toml gives five described anchors for six likert craft rows.
task/tests/scoring.toml:1-11 gives functionality 0.6 and craft 0.4, but no paired better/worse app run establishes monotone ordering. The persistence undervaluation is recorded in row 44.
task/tests/scoring.toml:1-11 gives gates zero mass and functional floor 0.05; task/tests/test.sh:213-227 runs gate suite and score.py before scored suite.

task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml hro_restart assigns 0.5 of the 45 functional weight total; task/tests/scoring.toml:5-11 makes that only 0.0067 of total possible reward. Losing every operational write on process restart is a core contract breach (instruction.md:1,5,13), yet costs under 1%.
quality.counterexample: A memory-only app with every other criterion perfect scores 1 - 0.6*(0.5/45) = 0.9933 despite violating persistent storage and audit retention.
quality.suggested_fix: Increase persistence weight substantially or strengthen a gate with true process-restart evidence while preserving independent credit for other functionality.
